## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13340 compaction trigger fires at wrong threshold — HIGH PRIORITY NEW (SMALL ~4-5h, CONFIRMED bug)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #13340 "fix(cli): trigger auto-compaction at the configured context threshold" fixed compaction trigger to fire at the correct threshold. Two bugs: (1) **Wrong base for percentage**: threshold_percent was applied to `model.limit.input || model.limit.context` instead of `model.limit.context`. For models with separate input limits (GPT-5: 272k input of 400k context window), "80%" threshold was really 54% of the displayed bar. (2) **Inflated estimate as trigger**: compared limit against char-based estimate of whole payload (`chars/4 × 1.3` + tool schemas) instead of provider-reported input tokens + tail estimate. Dense content (CJK, minified JS, disassembly) tokenizes denser than 4 chars/token, so estimate under-counted and compaction never fired until provider rejected with context-window-exceeded. Fix: (1) Apply threshold_percent to `model.limit.context` (the denominator UI uses), (2) Track provider-reported input token count (`reported`), (3) Estimate tokens added since last assistant reply (`tail`, 1.3× inflated estimate of new messages), (4) Trigger on `reported + tail` exceeds threshold (falls back to full estimate on first turn or post-compaction when no baseline exists). **Verified Alexi has the bug**: (1) `src/core/catalog.ts` ModelInfo only has `contextWindow` field (line 25), NO separate `inputLimit` or `maxInputTokens` field, so Alexi cannot apply threshold to context window separately from input limit (Kilocode bug #1 NOT DIRECTLY APPLICABLE because Alexi does not track input vs context limits separately, but compaction still uses wrong denominator if input limit differs). (2) `src/core/compaction.ts` `shouldCompact` (line 182-204) applies `thresholdPercent` to `maxContextTokens` (line 198-201), uses `estimateMessagesTokens(messages)` (line 200) which falls back to chars/4 (line 164), NO provider-reported baseline (`reported`) or tail estimate. `src/core/sessionManager.ts` line 648 calls `shouldCompact(this.activeSession!.messages, this.maxContextTokens)` with NO reported-token or tail parameters. `src/core/orchestrator.ts` and `src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts` capture `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` / `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` but NOT `usage.input_tokens` or `usage.promptTokens` (AI SDK exposes `usage.promptTokens` on response, not stored anywhere). **Kilocode bug #2 CONFIRMED** — Alexi compaction trigger uses character estimate only, no provider-reported baseline, no tail projection.

- **Why**: Dense content (CJK, minified sources, disassembly, base64) tokenizes denser than 4 chars/token. Alexi compaction uses character estimate only, no provider-reported token count, no tail projection. Compaction never fires for dense transcripts until provider rejects with context-window-exceeded, and affected turns get squeezed to tiny output budgets. This is HIGH PRIORITY — compaction failures cause user-visible quality degradation (tiny output budgets, repeated context-window errors, session unusability on dense content). Implementation cost ~4-5h: (1) Add `inputLimit?: number` field to ModelInfo interface in `src/core/catalog.ts` (5 lines, optional field, defaults to `contextWindow` when absent), update default model catalog entries for GPT-5 family if we have them (10 lines, check current catalog for GPT-5 models with 272k input / 400k context), (2) Update `shouldCompact` in `src/core/compaction.ts` to accept `reported?: number` and `tail?: number` parameters (20 lines, add optional params, trigger on `max(estimate, reported + tail)` when reported is present, fall back to estimate-only when absent), (3) Capture `usage.promptTokens` from provider responses in `src/core/orchestrator.ts` and `src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts` (15 lines, AI SDK already exposes `usage.promptTokens` on response, store it on message `tokens.input`), (4) Track `reportedInputTokens` on session metadata in `src/core/sessionManager.ts` (10 lines, add field to SessionMetadata, update on message add), (5) Compute tail estimate in `src/core/sessionManager.ts` compaction trigger (25 lines, estimate tokens of messages added since last assistant reply, apply 1.3× safety factor, pass `reported` and `tail` to `shouldCompact`), (6) Add tests for dense content compaction trigger (30 lines, verify CJK/minified JS triggers compaction correctly, verify tail projection works). Total ~115 lines, ~4-5h. Carry-forward lower-priority items from 2026-09-17/2026-09-18 (Cline #14195 actual token count, similar fix, now superseded by this Kilocode fix which is more comprehensive).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13340 (Kilocode compaction threshold fix, merged 2026-09-18), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/catalog.ts (Alexi ModelInfo line 20-31, VERIFIED only has `contextWindow`, no `inputLimit`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/compaction.ts (Alexi `shouldCompact` line 182-204, VERIFIED uses char estimate only, no `reported` or `tail`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi compaction trigger line 648, VERIFIED no reported-token or tail parameters)

- **Category**: core (compaction, context-window handling, token estimation)

- **Size**: SMALL (~4-5h). HIGH PRIORITY. Add `inputLimit` to ModelInfo, update `shouldCompact` to accept `reported` + `tail`, capture `usage.promptTokens`, track `reportedInputTokens` on session, compute tail estimate, trigger on `max(estimate, reported + tail)`, add dense-content tests. NEW finding 2026-09-19, CONFIRMED bug.

#### 2. Cline #14195 compaction trigger using actual token count — SUPERSEDED (carry-forward from 2026-09-18, now lower priority)

- **What**: Cline PR #14195 (carry-forward from 2026-09-18 research) is the same compaction bug as Kilocode #13340, but Kilocode's fix is more comprehensive (includes input vs context limit distinction, tail projection with 1.3× safety factor, and reasoning-model encrypted content handling). Cline fix: records `previousRequestInputTokens`, triggers on `max(estimate, actual)`, scales retention budget by `max(1, actual / estimate)`. Kilocode fix: tracks `reported` baseline, computes `tail` estimate of new content, triggers on `reported + tail`, applies threshold to context window not input limit.

- **Why**: Kilocode #13340 (finding #1 above) is the better reference implementation — it solves the same bug PLUS handles input vs context limit distinction and tail projection. Cline #14195 is still valid but now LOWER PRIORITY (Kilocode fix is more complete). When implementing, use Kilocode's approach (reported + tail) instead of Cline's (max(estimate, actual)).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14195 (Cline compaction trigger fix), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13340 (Kilocode compaction threshold fix, BETTER reference)

- **Category**: core (compaction, superseded by Kilocode #13340)

- **Size**: SKIP (superseded by finding #1, use Kilocode approach instead). Carry-forward from 2026-09-18, now LOWER PRIORITY.

#### 4. Cline #14171 Windows CWD security — MEDIUM PRIORITY (carry-forward from 2026-09-18, CONFIRMED)

- **What**: Cline PR #14171 (carry-forward from 2026-09-18 research) disabled Windows CWD executable search (libuv resolves bare program names on Windows by searching child's working directory before PATH; malicious repo can ship fake `rg.exe` or `git.exe` and get it executed). Fix: set `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` env var at startup (Microsoft documented opt-out, honored by libuv, cmd.exe, Go, Bun 1.4+). **Verified Alexi lacks the hardening** (2026-09-18 research, grep for `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` found zero matches).

- **Why**: Security hardening. Malicious repo can ship fake `rg.exe` / `git.exe` and get it executed by Alexi on Windows at file-search or git operation time. Implementation cost ~2h: (1) Add `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()` helper in `src/utils/process.ts` (~20 lines, Windows-only, sets `process.env.NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1'`), (2) Call at startup in `src/cli/program.ts` (1 line), (3) Add Windows-only test (30 lines, plant zero-byte `cmd.exe` in temp dir, assert real one runs). MEDIUM PRIORITY — security hardening, low likelihood (requires malicious repo + Windows + Alexi) but high impact (arbitrary code execution). Carry-forward from 2026-09-18, CONFIRMED.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14171 (Cline Windows CWD security fix), 2026-09-18 research verification

- **Category**: tools (security, Windows, spawn safety)

- **Size**: SMALL (~2h). MEDIUM PRIORITY. Add helper, call at startup, add test. Carry-forward from 2026-09-18, CONFIRMED.

#### 9. Cline #14274 CLI ask-question text input — NOT APPLICABLE (Cline OpenTUI vs Alexi Ink)

- **What**: Cline PR #14274 "fix(cli): preserve ask-question text input" fixed ask-question text input to preserve capitalization and Unicode (previously inline ask-question responses reconstructed printable text from OpenTUI's normalized key name, lost capitalization on shifted letters like `A` -> `a`, malformed Unicode on backspace; fix uses keyboard event's printable sequence so committed text keeps capitalization, punctuation, spaces, Unicode; backspace now removes one complete grapheme, preserving supplementary characters, combining marks, flags, joined emoji). This is a Cline CLI TUI bug fix (Cline uses OpenTUI for CLI rendering, OpenTUI normalizes keyboard events to key names, loses printable sequence info).

- **Why**: Cline CLI TUI implementation detail. Alexi uses Ink + ink-text-input for TUI rendering, NOT OpenTUI. Ink's `useInput` hook receives raw keyboard events and passes printable sequences directly to text input components (ink-text-input handles capitalization, Unicode, grapheme deletion correctly by default). Alexi does not have the keyboard event reconstruction bug (different TUI architecture). NOT APPLICABLE to Alexi (Cline uses OpenTUI, Alexi uses Ink, different keyboard event handling).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14274 (Cline CLI ask-question text input fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/components/ControlledTextInput.tsx (Alexi uses ink-text-input, line 1-200 imports `import TextInput from 'ink-text-input'`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/components/InputBox.tsx (Alexi input component, uses Ink, not OpenTUI)
